_about: Maps the original's <EntityName> strings onto gameplay ROLES.
This mapping is OUR design decision, which is why it lives here and not in the
converter: the converter is a data pipeline and emits the raw name as node metadata
(metadata/entity_name), leaving interpretation to the game. CLAUDE.md rule 1.
Names are matched EXACTLY against metadata/entity_name. The original writes the same
logical entity both bare and with a .ent suffix, and those are genuinely DIFFERENT
entities with different inline bodies (e.g. inline 'crate' has density 0.2 while
crate.ent has 0.4), so both spellings are listed where both occur. Do not collapse
Anything not listed here is scenery: it still converts, renders and collides, it just

A name may appear in only ONE role. LevelRuntime flattens this into {name: role}, so a duplicate silently resolves to whichever role is read last - which is how no_portal_sign.ent once ended up counted as scenery while being listed as a portal zone. LevelRuntime now warns on duplicates rather than picking one quietly.

player_spawn._note: Where the character starts. Present in all 32 chapter-1 scenes.

camera_start._note: Initial camera position. Corroborated by readCameraStartPos in the bytecode.

_note: Far corner of the playable area; present in all 32 scenes. Paired with the
minX/maxX/minY/maxY custom-data keys seen on some levels, and with
clampCameraPos in the bytecode.
Carries per-level settings in custom data - notably max_portals, the portal
budget. Only 6 of 32 chapter-1 scenes place one; absent means 'use defaults'.

exit_door._note: The level exit. In all 32 scenes. shape=0, so its <Collision> box is a trigger.

_note: Crystals. 106 placements across 28 of 32 chapter-1 scenes - the most-placed
gameplay entity. Bytecode has crystalCounter / _numCrystals / getCrystalCount.
Kills on contact - ETHBeginContactCallback_death_area in the bytecode. sensor=1.
Only one placement in chapter 1 (an early level), many more in later worlds.
Pre-placed portals. Custom data carries index, destiny (the index it links TO),
color (blue/red) and active. So static portals are explicitly PAIRED in the data
rather than inferred - see docs/ethanon-formats.md.
Regions where the player may not place a portal. antiportal carries a 'scale'
multiplier; the bytecode has isPointInAntiPortalField and AntiPortalManager.
no_portal_sign.ent is deliberately NOT here - it is signage marking where a zone is, with the same speed/stride hint animation as the other tutorial graphics. It lives in scenery_hint.
anti_portal_agent is NOT here either, since the remaster record's step 126 (00_order R17): the
original's agent refuses nothing. AntiPortalManager's constructor gathers its fields from
GetEntityArray('antiportal') and ('antiportal.ent') alone (bytes 104925..105343 #16-37), so
no tap is tested against an agent. It has a role of its own, below.
The red orb that holds a ring open: 21 placements on 17 levels, both spellings, one
callback (ETHCallback_anti_portal_agent, bytes 336011..337087). It has no shape and
refuses no portal. A portal shot still in flight within 0.7 x its size deletes the shot
and the agent, and the agent deletes the one antiportal round it
(deleteAntiPortalInThisBucket), so where the ring was a portal may open. Its numbers are
the port's placement.json `anti_portal_agent`. The ones with a speed and a stride patrol
(linearMotion, #200-250): two in level10 and one in level13b. Remaster record, step 126.
Oscillates VERTICALLY. speed is a FREQUENCY and stride a
distance in pixels (they are inversely correlated so speed*stride is near-constant).
Only the inline 'moving_platform' is live: ETHCallback_moving_platform exists, but
ETHCallback_moving_platform_single / _platform / _anchor do NOT, so those are INERT
and their custom data is dead copy-paste. Do not animate them.
Vertical shuttle. 'a' and 'b' are ENTITY NAMES of invisible marker
entities (liftA/liftB, or liftA2/liftB2 where a level has two). The lift spawns on 'a'.

lift_marker._note: Invisible endpoint markers referenced by lift.a / lift.b.

_note: Pressure plate. 'idx' is the channel; pairs with a switched door's
'switchIdx'. NOT a latch - the original counts touching entities and has both begin-
and end-contact callbacks, so it releases as soon as the last body leaves.
Opens while its channel is pressed. 'stride' is a bare uint
with no 'speed', so it is MILLISECONDS (300-16000), not a distance.
plane = vertical|horizontal. GUESS as to what it reflects; the
binary has both portal_reflect.mp3 and projectile_reflect.mp3.
Tutorial hint graphics. All shape=0 (no collision) with
identical hard-coded speed/stride on every placement - purely cosmetic, and a wrong
animation here cannot break a puzzle.
The draggable handle (planning step 139; the port's game/data/handle.json, sim/Handle). Filed as
scenery_hint, 'purely cosmetic', until then; it is not: a touch that goes down on it drags it one for
one with the finger, 64 units a frame at most (ETHCallback_arrows, listing L67305), and the fire agent
or reflector whose `follow` names it eases after it (doFollow, L67201) - the only way to bring a flame
to 2-20's crates. Six placements, one on each of 2-20 to 2-24 and 2-27, each on its follower's point.

demolisher._note: Destroys anything flagged `breakable` on contact. demolisher=1 on all 27 placements.

_note: Inert on contact - no ETHBeginContactCallback_barrel_bomb exists, only a per-frame
emissive pulse. Detonation is REQUESTED by a fireball, fire or another explosion.

fire_source._note: Permanent open flame; ignites burnable and detonates explosive in reach.

shock_field._note: Lethal ring of radius areaRadius, drawn so the danger zone is honest.

gravity_well._note: Local gravity well of radius `radius`. Chapter 4 (zero-g) only.

turret._note: Carranca - a wall-mounted gargoyle spitting fireballs along (dirX,dirY).

launcher._note: Spawns `entity` every `stride` ms; min/max is a cull box.

key._note: Carryable, colour-paired with keyhole and locked door.

keyhole._note: Consumes a same-colour key and removes every same-colour locked door.

locked_door._note: Solid until a same-colour key reaches its keyhole.

_note: Invisible marker. No enemy is ever placed directly in a scene.
waypointName is a PREFIX: 'wayA' patrols wayA0 <-> wayA1.

waypoint._note: Patrol markers. holdTime is MILLISECONDS; 9999999 means a stationary guard.

_note: Revolute joints. Data is nested inside <Collision>, like <Polygon> and
<Compound>. Angles are RADIANS - the shipped +-1.57075 is +-pi/2. 10 instances, worlds 2-4.
Exactly one per chapter, always level 32. 1-32 adder (entity:beholder.ent),
2-32 dragon.ent, 3-32 ghost_pos, 4-32 dark_dragon_spawn.
STRUCTURE only - the attack patterns are bespoke AngelScript we can name but not read.
Solid polygon surface that throws things off it. 64x64, shape=3,
static, non-sensor - so it is real geometry, not a trigger. ETHCallback_bounce exists.
64x128 with shape=0 and NO sprite - an invisible barrier that
stops projectiles but not the player. Pairs with anti_sight_wall in the same family.
Diamonds. Separate from crystals: shock_diamond_pick.mp3 exists as its own
cue, and ETHCallback_shock_diamond / _fire_diamond are distinct callbacks.
Chapter 4's unlit levels ('darkest'). An unlit torch that can be switched on;
'switch' custom data on the 4 inline ones. This is what makes the dark levels navigable.
4-19's red halo on the red key (level18c places the one in the game, on key_2701's
point). NOT scenery: ETHCallback_red_key_state (Enhanced's out/parity/asbc/
all_functions.txt L97171) plays playRedKeyGotSound once the key in its bucket is
taken (#224-277), fades its own colour and the level's ambient light to nothing over
6000 ms (#88-178), and then destroys SeekEntity('breakable_wall') (#190-220) - the
wall between the key and the rocket. Filed under scenery_fx as 'a HUD-ish indicator'
until planning step 118; game/sim/RedKey.hpp plays it.
Decoration and boss parts with a live ETHCallback but no gameplay consequence.
Classified explicitly so the coverage sweep reports ZERO unexplained entities rather
than a list someone has to re-triage.
hand_waypoint0              - 2-20's lesson hand (see scenery_hint; its callback is handle.json's
lesson). arrows.ent, filed beside it until step 139, is `handle`
gutter_mouth.ent            - a wall spout; decorative drip emitter
dragon_claw.ent             - part of the chapter-2 boss, which is a placeholder
rocket_launch / _landing    - the anchors of 4-01's and 4-19's win cutscenes, acting only
after the door (the medal's delay is the level's end_delay;
the port's game/data/cutscenes.json)
(red_key_state.ent was filed here until planning step 118: it is its own role above.)
